stem:
A student investigates a circuit containing a capacitor and a resistor as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A dual-beam oscilloscope is connected across the capacitor of capacitance *C* and resistor of resistance *R*. The oscilloscope displays two traces as shown in Fig. 2.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The student determines the phase difference *θ* between the two traces.

The student repeats the experiment with different resistors.

It is suggested that *θ* and *R* are related by the equation

$\tan θ = \frac{1}{2πfCR}$

where *f* is the frequency of the a.c. power supply.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of tan *θ* on the y-axis against 1/*R* on the x-axis.

Determine an expression for the gradient.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *R* and *θ* are given in Table 2.1.

Each value of *R* has a percentage uncertainty of ±5%.

[[fig:f3]]

Calculate and record values of 1/*R* / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹ and tan *θ* in Table 2.1.

Include the absolute uncertainties in 1/*R*.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of tan *θ* against 1/*R* / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹.

Include error bars for 1/*R*.

[[fig:f4]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The student measured the frequency of the a.c. power supply twice. The student’s values were 101 Hz and 97 Hz.

Determine the average frequency *f* of the power supply. Include the absolute uncertainty in *f*.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(ii) and (d), determine the value of *C*. Include an appropriate unit.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
The experiment is repeated using the same power supply and capacitor.

Determine the resistance of *R* that would give a phase difference of 40°. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A circuit with an a.c. power supply, a capacitor and a resistor, with connections to a dual-beam oscilloscope.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.2
figures.alt: A graph grid showing two sinusoidal traces with different phases.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for resistance, reciprocal resistance, phase difference and tan θ; it gives resistance values 12, 16, 22, 33, 39 and 43 Ω and phase differences 80.8°, 77.5°, 73.0°, 65.2°, 61.7° and 59.3°.
A blank graph grid with tan θ on the vertical axis, marked from 1.0 to 6.5, and 1/R / 10⁻³ Ω⁻¹ on the horizontal axis, marked from 20 to 90.
